question.text: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted from a metal surface increases from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math> when the frequency of the incident radiation is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo>%</mo></math>. What is the work function (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>eV</mi></math>) of the metal surface?

solution.text:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation,

Kmax=hυ-ϕ0

where Kmax is the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons and ϕ0 is the work function of the metal surface

Initially,

hυ=0.4+ϕ0

When the frequency is increased by 40%, then

1.4hυ=1.2+ϕ0

On solving we get

ϕ0=1.6 eV
